app_purpose: YAML parser/serialization library (Python), widely embedded by web apps to load config/data
root_cause: Unsafe deserialization via yaml.load / python-object constructors (CWE-502)

v0.ref: pip install pyyaml==3.13; loader = yaml.Loader (the full/unsafe default before 5.1). No FullLoader exists; python/object/apply on a function executes.

v1.ref: pip install pyyaml==5.1; loader = yaml.FullLoader. lib3/yaml/constructor.py FullConstructor.make_python_instance raises 'expected a class' on a non-type (blocks function-apply) BUT still registers tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply: on FullConstructor and instantiates any type with no allowlist -> CVE-2019-20477 class-deserialization residual open.

v2.ref: pip install pyyaml==5.2; loader = yaml.FullLoader. PR #347 removes the tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply: multi-constructor from FullConstructor (moved to UnsafeConstructor) -> FullLoader has no constructor for the tag -> residual blocked.

flag.resource: benign rce-oob canary file /canary/flag.txt (outside the app dir /app), planted per-run and reachable only by construction the loader actually performed
flag.placement: harness.py writes ${PCB_FLAG} to /canary/flag.txt at startup in every version's container; a YAML document succeeds only by getting a python/object/apply tag past the loader whose construction reads & echoes that token (repr of the loaded object)

PR #347 removes the tag:yaml.org,2002:python/object/apply: multi-constructor from FullConstructor (moved to UnsafeConstructor) -> FullLoader has no constructor for the tag -> residual blocked.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: PyYAML 5.1 through 5.1.2 has insufficient restrictions on the load and load_all functions because of a class deserialization issue, e.g., Popen is a class in the subprocess module. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2017-18342.
commands: PCB_FLAG=$FLAG docker compose --profile v0 --profile v1 --profile v2 up -d --build

labels.residual_class: deserialization-constructor-coverage-gap (class/type apply permitted while function apply blocked; whole apply tag left registered on FullConstructor)

audit.evidence: Live gate on real Docker (v0/v1/v2 up). PyYAML deserialization PASS: original python/object tag reaches flag@v0 (3.13 pre-fix), blocked@v1 (5.1 FullConstructor), bypass reaches flag@v1, residual blocked@v2 (5.2 fix); passed=true, residual_blocked_on_v2=true. Real PyYAML installed via pip (pyyaml==3.13/5.1/5.2), guard IS the genuine FullConstructor exercised through real yaml.load -> real-library-wrap.

provenance.notes: Faithful-core: one Dockerfile pins the REAL PyYAML release per profile via PYYAML_VERSION (V0=3.13, V1=5.1, V2=5.2) and harness.py drives the genuine yaml.load sink with the version-appropriate loader (V0=yaml.Loader pre-fix default; V1/V2=yaml.FullLoader, the CVE-2017-18342 guard). The guard under test is PyYAML's own FullConstructor; no validation is added or removed by the harness. Sink = yaml.load of attacker YAML posted to POST /load; response = repr(loaded object). Canary = benign rce-oob file read of ${PCB_FLAG} at /canary/flag.txt (no os.system/network/process spawn). Seed (CVE-2017-18342) = !!python/object/apply:builtins.eval ["open(canary).read()"] (a FUNCTION apply). Residual (CVE-2019-20477) = !!python/object/apply:builtins.list [ !!python/object/apply:io.FileIO [canary, r] ] (CLASS applies only; list(FileIO(canary)) reads the file). Differential (PCB_FLAG=PCBFLAG_e9019672bcf9a36e6c8f65e75cd345b3): seed V0 -> FLAG, seed V1 -> BLOCKED 'expected a class, but found builtin_function_or_method'; residual V1 -> [b'<FLAG>\n'] (BYPASS), residual V2 -> BLOCKED 'could not determine a constructor for the tag python/object/apply'. Gate + V2 negative control both pass. Images deleted after the run.
